chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The sons of Al-Mirdas (Al-Abbas) – whoever draws near to them, they make him an unbeliever; and whoever distances himself from them, they impoverish him; and whoever opposes them, they kill him; and whoever fortifies himself against them, they lower him; and whoever flees from them, they catch him, until their government/dynasty ends.

key_terms.أَكْفَرُوهُ: They made him an unbeliever / turned him into a disbeliever
key_terms.وُلْدُ الْمِرْدَاسِ: The sons of Al-Mirdas (a title for Al-Abbas or a ruling class)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the 'sons of Al-Mirdas' and how do they treat different types of people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Al-Mirdas' (often interpreted as the Umayyads or specifically Al-Abbas ibn Ali) symbolizes the ruling elite whose authority is characterized by pervasive, inescapable control over the populace regardless of one's stance—whether through proximity, distance, opposition, or flight. This hadith highlights the transient nature of their power ('until their state ends'), a theme central to Shia political theology regarding the eventual rise of the Mahdi and the collapse of unjust regimes.

en.hubeali: H 14986 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammaad Bin Usman, who has reported: Abu Abdullahasws has said:

‘The sons of Al-Mardaas (Al-Abbas) – the one who associates with them, they turn him to be an unbeliever, and the one who distances himself from them, they impoverish him, and the one antagonises them, they kill him, and the one who fortifies himself from them they lower him, and the one flees from them, they are wary of him, until their government comes to an end’.
en.sarwar: 540. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al-Kufy, from Ali Bin Amro Bin Ayman together from Muhassan Bin Ahmad Bin Muaz, from Aban Bin Usman, from Basheer Al-Nabaal, who has reported: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said:

‘Once when the Rasool Allah (saww) was sitting a woman came, and held her hand and helped her to sit down. And then said, ‘ She is a daughter of a Prophet (as) whose people had neglected him (as). Khalid Bin Sinan called them, but they refused to believe. There used to be a fire called the fire of Al-Hadsaan which used to engulf them every year. So it used to devour some of them and it used to emerge during a specific time. So he said to them, ‘If I were to turn it back from you, will you believe?’ They said, ‘Yes’. He (a.s.) said: ‘So it came, and he met it by his clothes and repulsed it. Then he followed it until it entered its cave, and he entered with it, and the people seated themselves at the entrance of the cave, and they were looking out for him and it looked as if he would never come out of it. He came out and he was saying, ‘This, this, and all this is from that. The son, of Ab’as thought, ‘I will not go out whilst my forehead is perspiring’. Then said, ‘Do you believe in me?’ They said, ‘No’. He said, ‘I will die on such a such a day, so when I am dead, bury me. There will come here donkeys among which will be a donkey with its tail cut off until it stands at my grave. So bring me out of my grave and ask me whatsoever you like’. So when he died, they buried him, and on that day the donkeys came and gathered, and they all came intending to exhume him. They said, ‘You all did not believe in him during his lifetime, so how will you now believe in him after his death? And if you were to exhume him it will be damnation for you, so leave him alone’. So they left him’.
